subject: How to plot a histogram with Density instead of Count on the y-axis?

messages.author: 3b57c7c8127a7e12
messages.subject: How to plot a histogram with Density instead of Count on the y-axis?
parts:
Is there a way to tell ggvis to display density (count / length of the var) instead of count when plotting a histogram?
In addition, how to overlay a density curve on top of the histogram?

For example, I've generated plot (attached) using the following ggplot2 commands. 
How can I generate the same plot in ggvis?

library(ggplot2)

n = 100; p=0.5; mu=n*p; sigma=sqrt(n*p*(1-p))

# generate 5000 binomial rv's
r.binom = rbinom(5000, n, p)

# calculate the corresponding normal densities
p.norm = dnorm(r.binom, mu, sigma)

# combine into a data.frame
dat = data.frame(r.binom, p.norm)

ggplot(dat, aes(r.binom)) + 
        geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), binwidth = 1, 
                       fill = hcl(h = 195, l = 65, c = 100), color = "black") +
        geom_line(aes(y = p.norm), 
                  color = hcl(h = 15, l = 65, c = 100), size = 1.2) + 
        theme_bw()
